newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies rally to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies rally to firmer close.

text.p: CME hog futures rallied after the December contract expiration and most months ended higher with pork bellies also rallying sharply by the close.
Lean hogs closed up 0.900 cent a lb to off 0.200 with February up most at 76.075 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.525 to 0.100 higher with February up 1.150 at 78.800 cents.

December hogs, the last live hog contract, fell for a limit loss of 1.500 cent a lb late before expiring at 58.500 cents, off 1.250 cents on the day. Deferred contracts then rallied as spillover pressure from the December contract was eliminated and traders looked to other market factors.

December was under liquidation pressure, partly linked to expectations that it would be much easier to deliver and market hogs next week as bitter cold weather departs the Midwest. Packer demand was also expected to be lighter next week due to the holiday, traders said.

But February and April rallied as the upcoming Hogs and Pigs report is expected to show tight hog numbers continuing into the first quarter of next year before climbing. Producers are holding back breeding stock now which will keep marketings light and the added production will start to effect prices later in the spring, they said.

Early estimates on the hog report pointed to all hogs on farms at 95 to 101 percent of a year ago with numbers kept for breeding estimated at 99.9 to 103 percent and hogs kept for market at 94 to 99 percent of last year.

Pork belly futures also rallied along with hog futures and finished up sharply at day's highs after falling early. Follow- through selling was lacking after early local pressure and long liquidation triggered sell stops under chart support, traders said.
Cash bellies will likely show a strong tone into early next year on projected light hog kills during the holidays.

Traders also cited projections for lighter-than-year-ago U.S. frozen stocks which added to the runup. Friday afternoon's monthly USDA Cold Storage Report is expected to show total U.S. belly stocks in November down from year-earlier levels and also below the 10-year November average.

Estimates on the report, to be released at 1400 CST, averaged 29 million lbs and ranged from 26.6 million to 32.2 million lbs. There were 37.092 million lbs in storage last year and a 10-year average on hand of 45.5 million lbs.
